Reasoning: Use Cartesian components for the electric field at the origin. Let E0 = kQ/r^2. method.method_draft: Use Cartesian component summation. From the image, identify the charge locations relative to the origin: +Q at (-r,0), +2Q at (+r,0), and -Q at (0,+r). From the text, use that each is distance r from the origin and the requested quantity is the magnitude of the electric field at the origin. Apply Coulomb field direction rules: field from a positive charge points away from the charge, field from a negative charge points toward the charge. Thus at the origin, +Q on the left gives +x field of magnitude kQ/r^2, +2Q on the right gives -x field of magnitude 2kQ/r^2, and -Q above gives +y field of magnitude kQ/r^2. Sum components to get Ex = -kQ/r^2 and Ey = +kQ/r^2, then take the magnitude sqrt(Ex^2+Ey^2)=sqrt(2)kQ/r^2.
